# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 23 ADRIAN TRELEAVEN COMES

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

A certain evening, Miss Winifred made a phone call down to Nell.
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0000 }

“That author chap has just gotten in. My plan is to chauffeur him over to where you are, which will allow you to direct him across to Lorna’s house. Taking that path cuts down the distance compared to taking the alternate route, plus I am in an extreme rush. Over at the Glen, the Coyle baby went and tumbled headfirst into a bucket filled with boiling water, ending up almost scalded to death, so my presence is requested immediately—to grow a fresh layer of skin on the infant, I imagine. Mrs. Coyle acts so negligently all the time, only to anticipate that everyone else will fix her errors. This won't bother you, will it, sweetheart? The luggage he brought can be brought down the next day.”
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0001 }

“All right,” Nell stated. “How would you describe him, Miss Winifred?”
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0002 }

“Once I bring him out, you will observe his exterior nature. Regarding his interior self, that is known solely to the Lord who created him. I refuse to speak anything further, because all the receivers throughout the Glen are out of order.”
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0003 }

“Miss Winifred clearly cannot discover many flaws in the appearance of Mr. Treleaven, or despite the receivers she would discover them,” Nell remarked. “Consequently, Tabitha, I infer that Mr. Treleaven is good-looking rather than the reverse.”
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0004 }

“Indeed, Mrs. Doctor, my dear, observing a handsome male brings me great pleasure,” Tabitha admitted openly. “Should I prepare a bit of food for him? A strawberry pie is available that is exceptionally tender.”
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0005 }

“No, Lorna expects him and already prepared his supper. Furthermore, I desire that strawberry pie for my own poor husband. He will not arrive home until a late hour, so set aside the pie and a glass of milk for him, Tabitha.”
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0006 }

“I certainly shall, Mrs. Doctor, dear. Tabitha is in control. Indeed, offering pie to your own people is preferable to giving it to unfamiliar folk, who might merely be trying to consume everything, and the doctor himself is as handsome an individual as one frequently encounters.”
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0007 }

Upon the arrival of Adrian Treleaven, Nell privately acknowledged, while Miss Winifred escorted him inside, that he was truly quite “well-looking”. He possessed a tall, broad-shouldered frame, complemented by dense brown hair, a sharp nose and chin, alongside expansive, luminous dark-gray eyes.
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0008 }

“Did you observe his teeth and his ears as well, Mrs. Doctor, dear?” Tabitha asked subsequently. “His ears have the most pleasing shape I have ever seen on any man. I am particular regarding ears. In my youth, I was terrified that I would be forced to wed a man possessing ears that resembled flaps. However, there was no reason for my anxiety, because I was never given an opportunity with a man having any type of ears.”
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0009 }

Although Nell failed to observe Adrian Treleaven’s ears, his teeth became visible to her when his lips separated in a candid, amiable smile. When he was not smiling, his countenance appeared somewhat sorrowful and distracted, resembling the somber, enigmatic protagonist of Nell’s former fantasies; however, laughter, wit, and attractiveness illuminated his features when he grinned. Indeed, externally, just as Miss Winifred remarked, Adrian Treleaven was a most attractive man.
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0010 }

“You cannot realize how delighted I am to be here, Mrs. Carrow,” he said, casting his gaze about with enthusiastic, curious eyes. “I have a strange sensation of returning home. As you know, my mother was born here and passed her youth here. She was accustomed to speak to me at great length about her former home. I am as familiar with its layout as with that of the place where I resided, and, naturally, she recounted to me the tale of the dwelling’s construction, along with my grandfather’s desperate vigil for the Royal William. I had assumed that a home so ancient would have disappeared long ago, otherwise I would have traveled to view it prior to now.”
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0011 }

“Along this bewitched shoreline, ancient homes fail to disappear with ease,” Nell stated with a smile. “A ‘land where all things always seem the same’ is what this place is—or almost always, anyway. The residence of John Tremayne has barely undergone any alterations, and right now, the rose-bushes that were planted by your grandfather for his bride are flowering outdoors.”
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0012 }

“That idea connects me to those people! With your permission, I need to check out the entire location before long.”
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0013 }

“You will always be welcome to visit us,” Nell pledged. “And are you aware that the former sea captain running the Seven Gulls lighthouse was acquainted with John Tremayne and his bride when he was young? He recounted their history to me on the evening I arrived at this place—the old house's third bride.”
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0014 }

“Is that even conceivable? This truly CONSTITUTES a find. I have to track him down.”
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0015 }

“It will not be hard; every one of us is an old friend of Captain Saul. His eagerness to meet you will match your own desire to meet him. In his mind, your grandmother glimmers like a star. However, it seems to me that Mrs. Vane awaits your arrival. I am going to point out our 'cross-lots’ path to you.”
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0016 }

Nell accompanied him to the home up the stream, crossing a pasture that held a snow-like whiteness from its daisies. A group of individuals in a boat sang far on the other side of the harbor. The audio floated across the water resembling soft, celestial melodies carried by the breeze over a sea beneath the stars. The large light shone and signaled. Adrian Treleaven surveyed his surroundings with contentment.
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0017 }

“So Seven Gulls is finally here,” he remarked. “Mother praised it so much, yet I was not expecting to encounter such immense beauty. The colors are so striking, the landscape so stunning, and the overall charm so delightful! My strength will surely return to me like a horse’s before long. Furthermore, if beauty serves as a spark for inspiration, this location will undoubtedly enable me to commence writing my major Canadian novel.”
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0018 }

“It hasn’t been started by you yet?” Nell inquired.
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0019 }

“Ah me, no. The correct core concept for it has always eluded me. It hides past my reach—it entices—and signals—and withdraws—I nearly hold it and it vanishes. It may be that surrounded by such tranquility and beauty, I will manage to seize it. I am told by Miss Tolley that you are a writer.”
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0020 }

“Oh, I write small pieces for young people. Since my marriage, I haven’t accomplished a great deal. Furthermore—a grand Canadian novel is not something I plan to attempt,” Nell chuckled. “Such a task is far past my abilities.”
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0021 }

Adrian Treleaven was also laughing.
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0022 }

“I suppose it surpasses my ability too. Even so, I intend to make an attempt at it eventually, provided I can find the time. An individual who works for a newspaper rarely gets an opportunity for that type of work. I have composed quite a few short stories for various magazines, yet I have lacked the free time that appears required to produce a book. However, given a three-month period of freedom, I should begin—if I were merely able to obtain the required theme for it—the SOUL of the work.”
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0023 }

A thought flashed across Nell’s mind so abruptly that it caused her to leap. Nevertheless, she kept it to herself, because the Vane residence had been reached. Just as they came into the yard, Lorna emerged onto the porch via the side entryway, squinting into the darkness to spot her anticipated visitor. The illuminated doorway cast a bath of golden radiance directly upon the spot where she paused. A simple outfit made of inexpensive, cream-colored cotton voile was what she had on, accompanied by her customary belt of crimson. Lorna was never seen lacking her splash of crimson. She had explained to Nell that contentment eluded her unless a spark of red adorned her somewhere, even if it was merely a single blossom. For Nell, this consistently appeared to signify Lorna’s vibrant, restrained character, which was refused any outlet except through that vivid flash. The neckline of Lorna’s dress was slightly lowered, and its sleeves were short. Ivory-colored marble seemed to shimmer in the form of her arms. Set against the illumination, every lovely contour of her figure stood out in gentle shadow. The light caused her hair to glisten like fire. Past her stretched a violet sky, blooming with stars above the harbor.
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0024 }

Nell listened as her partner let out a sharp breath. The shock and wonder filling his features remained visible to her, despite the gathering gloom.
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0025 }

“Which person is that stunning individual?” he inquired.
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0026 }

“Mrs. Vane is that lady,” Nell remarked. “She possesses great beauty, doesn’t she?”
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0027 }

“I—I have never witnessed anyone quite like her,” he replied, somewhat bewilderedly. “I was not ready—I had not anticipated—good lord, a person DOES NOT anticipate a goddess as a landlady! Really, were she dressed in a sea-purple robe, holding a string of amethysts within her hair, she would truly be a genuine sea-queen. And she accepts boarders!”
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0028 }

“All goddesses still have to survive,” Nell remarked. “Besides, Lorna is no goddess. She is simply an exceptionally lovely woman, every bit as human as we are. Has Miss Tolley informed you concerning Mr. Vane?”
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0029 }

“Yes,—he is lacking in his intellect, or some such thing, is he not? However, she mentioned nothing concerning Mrs. Vane, so I assumed she would be the typical bustling rural homemaker who accommodates guests to make a decent living.”
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0030 }

“Indeed, Lorna is engaged in that very action,” Nell stated sharply. “Furthermore, the situation is not entirely enjoyable for her, either. I trust Rufus will not bother you. Should he do so, kindly refrain from showing it to Lorna. Her feelings would be terribly injured. He is merely an oversized infant, and on occasion a somewhat vexing one.”
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0031 }

“Oh, I will not pay attention to him. I do not think I will spend much time inside the dwelling anyway, save to eat. Even so, what a pity the whole situation is! She must have a difficult existence.”
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0032 }

“That is correct. Nevertheless, she dislikes being felt sorry for.”
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0033 }

Lorna had returned inside the residence, and she now encountered them at the main entrance. She welcomed Adrian Treleaven with chilly politeness, informing him in a matter-of-fact voice that his chamber and his evening meal had been prepared for his arrival. Rufus, wearing a delighted smirk, shuffled up the stairs carrying the traveling bag, and Adrian Treleaven was settled as a resident of the ancient dwelling amid the willows.
{: #nw-v04-c23-p0034 }
